extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and United States Patent and Trademark Office officials
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory and regulatory requirements governing PTO advisory committees, boards, filings, practice before the Office, and the schedule and policies for patent-related fees. Covers composition, duties, meeting rules, evidence/submissions, revival and suspension procedures, and detailed fee schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of Patent and Trademark Public Advisory Committees
rubrics_metrics.description: The United States Patent and Trademark Office shall have a Patent Public Advisory Committee and a Trademark Public Advisory Committee, each with nine voting members appointed by the Secretary of Commerce who serve at the Secretary's pleasure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In each year, 3 members shall be appointed to each Advisory Committee for 3-year terms beginning on December 1 of that year. Any vacancy shall be filled within 90 days; a new member filling a vacancy serves the remainder of the predecessor's term. The Secretary, in consultation with the Director, shall designate a Chair and Vice Chair from among the members; the Vice Chair shall exercise the Chair's functions if the Chair resigns or is unable to act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for Advisory Committee appointments – citizenship and representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of each Advisory Committee shall be citizens of the United States chosen to represent the interests of diverse users of the USPTO with respect to patents (Patent Public Advisory Committee) and trademarks (Trademark Public Advisory Committee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appointments must represent diverse users; membership should reflect differing stakeholder interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small-entity representation on Patent Public Advisory Committee
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisory Committee membership shall include members who represent small and large entity applicants in proportion to applications filed, but members representing small entity patent applicants must constitute not less than 25 percent of the Patent Public Advisory Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such small-entity representatives shall include at least one independent inventor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications and backgrounds for Advisory Committee members
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisory Committees shall include individuals with substantial background and achievement in finance, management, labor relations, science, technology, and office automation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to voting members, each Advisory Committee shall include a representative of each labor organization recognized by the USPTO as nonvoting members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory Committee meetings and openness
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Advisory Committee shall meet at the call of the chair to consider an agenda set by the chair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meetings shall be open to the public except that an Advisory Committee may by majority vote meet in executive session when considering personnel, privileged, or other confidential information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory Committee duties — review and advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Advisory Committee shall review the policies, goals, performance, budget, and user fees of the USPTO (with respect to patents for the Patent Public Advisory Committee, and trademarks for the Trademark Public Advisory Committee) and advise the Director on these matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further required actions: within 60 days after the end of each fiscal year, prepare an annual report on these matters, transmit the report to the Secretary of Commerce, the President, and the Judiciary Committees of the Senate and House, and publish the report in the Official Gazette of the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory Committee compensation and travel
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Advisory Committee member shall be compensated for each day (including travel time) attending meetings or otherwise engaged in business of the Advisory Committee at the daily equivalent of the annual rate for Level III of the Executive Schedule under 5 U.S.C. 5314.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While away from home or regular place of business, such members shall be allowed travel expenses, including per diem in lieu of subsistence, as authorized by 5 U.S.C. 5703.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory Committee access to information
rubrics_metrics.description: Members shall be provided access to records and information in the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: personnel or other privileged information and information concerning patent applications required to be kept in confidence by section 122.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory Committee ethics/status provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of each Advisory Committee shall be special Government employees within the meaning of section 202 of title 18.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 4 (patent prohibition) does not apply to voting members of the Advisory Committees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Advisory Committee Act inapplicability
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal Advisory Committee Act (5 U.S.C. App.) shall not apply to each Advisory Committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment and composition of the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB)
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be in the Office a Patent Trial and Appeal Board consisting of the Director, Deputy Director, Commissioner for Patents, Commissioner for Trademarks, and the administrative patent judges (APJs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative patent judges shall be persons of competent legal knowledge and scientific ability appointed by the Secretary in consultation with the Director. References to the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences are deemed to refer to the PTAB under the current statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB duties — appeal and review authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The PTAB shall: (1) on written appeal of an applicant, review adverse decisions of examiners upon patent applications pursuant to section 134(a); (2) review appeals of reexaminations pursuant to section 134(b); (3) conduct derivation proceedings pursuant to section 135; and (4) conduct inter partes reviews and post-grant reviews pursuant to chapters 31 and 32.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-member panels for PTAB proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Each appeal, derivation proceeding, post-grant review, and inter partes review shall be heard by at least 3 members of the PTAB designated by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the PTAB may grant rehearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of prior appointments and de facto officer defense
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary may deem appointments of administrative patent judges who previously held office pursuant to appointment by the Director to take effect on the date the Director initially appointed the judge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It shall be a defense to a challenge to the appointment of an administrative patent judge on the basis of prior appointment by the Director that the judge was acting as a de facto officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance of a PTO library
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall maintain a library of scientific and other works and periodicals, foreign and domestic, in the Patent and Trademark Office to aid officers in the discharge of their duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of patents by subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may revise and maintain the classification by subject matter of U.S. letters patent and other patents and printed publications for determining novelty of inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Furnishing certified copies of records
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may furnish certified copies of specifications and drawings of patents issued by the USPTO, and of other records available to the public or to the person applying for them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publications the Director may publish
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may publish in printed, typewritten, or electronic form: patents and published applications (specifications and drawings), certificates of trademark registrations, the Official Gazette, annual indexes of patents/patentees and trademarks/registrants, annual volumes of decisions, and pamphlet copies of patent laws, rules, and related circulars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may exchange certain publications with desirable publications for Office use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exchange of copies of patents and applications with foreign countries
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may exchange copies of specifications and drawings of U.S. patents and published applications for those of foreign countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director shall not enter into such an agreement to provide copies to a foreign country (other than a USMCA country or a WTO member country) without express authorization of the Secretary of Commerce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Providing copies to public libraries
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may supply copies of specifications and drawings of patents and published applications in printed or electronic form to public libraries in the United States for public use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies are supplied at the rate for each year's issue established under section 41(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual report to Congress timing and content
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall report to Congress not later than 180 days after the end of each fiscal year the moneys received and expended by the Office, the purposes for which the moneys were spent, the quality and quantity of the work of the Office, the nature of training provided to examiners, the evaluation of the Commissioner of Patents and the Commissioner of Trademarks by the Secretary of Commerce, the compensation of the Commissioners, and other information relating to the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date rule related to United States Postal Service deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may by rule prescribe that any paper or fee required to be filed in the PTO will be considered filed on the date it was deposited with the United States Postal Service or would have been deposited but for postal interruptions or emergencies designated by the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: When action day falls on weekend or Federal holiday
rubrics_metrics.description: When the day, or the last day, for taking any action or paying any fee in the USPTO falls on Saturday, Sunday, or a Federal holiday within DC, the action may be taken, or fee paid, on the next succeeding secular or business day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printing/typewriting/electronic requirements for papers filed
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may require papers filed in the USPTO to be printed, typewritten, or on an electronic medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpoenas and witness attendance in PTO contested cases
rubrics_metrics.description: The clerk of any U.S. district court for the district where testimony is to be taken shall, upon application, issue a subpoena for any witness residing or being within such district to appear and testify before an authorized officer; Federal Rules of Civil Procedure relating to attendance and production apply to contested PTO cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Witnesses are allowed fees and traveling expenses as in U.S. district courts. A judge may enforce obedience or punish disobedience. No contempt for failing to obey unless fees/traveling expenses and one day's attendance are paid or tendered at service time; refusal to disclose secret matter only upon appropriate court order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration in lieu of oath
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may by rule prescribe that any document required to be under oath may be subscribed by a written declaration in a form the Director prescribes, in lieu of the oath.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whenever such written declaration is used, the document must warn the declarant that willful false statements are punishable by fine or imprisonment or both (18 U.S.C. 1001).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for affidavits/depositions and provisional acceptance of defective execution
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may establish rules for taking affidavits and depositions required in PTO cases; any officer authorized to take depositions for courts may take such affidavits and depositions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any document required to be executed in specified manner may be provisionally accepted by the Director despite defective execution, provided a properly executed document is submitted within such time as prescribed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revival of unintentionally abandoned applications and reinstatement of reexamination proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may establish procedures, including requirement for payment of the fee specified in section 41(a)(7), to revive an unintentionally abandoned application, accept an unintentionally delayed payment of the fee for issuing each patent, or accept an unintentionally delayed response by the patent owner in a reexamination proceeding, upon petition by the applicant or patent owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension or exclusion from practice before the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may, after notice and opportunity for hearing, suspend or exclude from further practice before the USPTO any person, agent, or attorney shown to be incompetent or disreputable, guilty of gross misconduct, not complying with regulations under section 2(b)(2)(D), or who, with intent to defraud, deceives, misleads, or threatens applicants or others having business before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons shall be recorded. The Director may designate any USPTO attorney to conduct the hearing. A proceeding must be commenced not later than the earlier of (a) 10 years after the date the misconduct occurred, or (b) 1 year after the date the misconduct is made known to an officer/employee of the Office as prescribed. Review of the Director's action may be in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unauthorized representation as practitioner penalty
rubrics_metrics.description: Whoever, not being recognized to practice before the USPTO, holds himself out or permits himself to be held out as so recognized, or as qualified to prepare or prosecute patent applications, shall be fined not more than $1,000 for each offense.

rubrics_metrics.name: General rule: Director shall charge patent-related fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall charge the fees set forth for filing, examination, issue, maintenance, searches, and other services related to patents and patent processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees are detailed in subsections and may be adjusted and subject to reductions for small entities and other rules described below.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing and basic national fees (amounts by application type)
rubrics_metrics.description: On filing each application for an original patent (except design, plant, or provisional) $330; original design patent $220; original plant patent $220; provisional application $220; reissue application $330; basic national fee for entering national stage under section 371 $330.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For specifications and drawings exceeding 100 sheets (or equivalent), $270 for each additional 50 sheets (or fraction thereof), excluding certain sequence or computer program listings filed electronically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess claims fees
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to filing fee: $220 for each independent claim in excess of 3; $52 for each claim (dependent or independent) in excess of 20; $390 for each application containing a multiple dependent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For computing fees, a multiple dependent claim referred to in section 112 or any claim depending therefrom is considered as separate dependent claims according to the number of claims referenced. The Director may by regulation provide refunds for canceled claims before examination on the merits and may rectify errors in payment under prescribed regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination fees (amounts by application type)
rubrics_metrics.description: For examination: original (utility) application $220; original design $140; original plant $170; national stage of international application $220; reissue examination $650.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisions of section 111(a) paragraphs (3) and (4) and section 371(d) apply to payment applicability as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue fees (amounts)
rubrics_metrics.description: For issuing each original patent (utility) $1,510; original design patent $860; original plant patent $1,190; issuing each reissue patent $1,510.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclaimer fee
rubrics_metrics.description: On filing each disclaimer, $140.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal fees
rubrics_metrics.description: On filing an appeal from the examiner to the PTAB, $540; on filing a brief in support of the appeal, $540; on requesting an oral hearing in the appeal before the PTAB, $1,080.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revival petition fee
rubrics_metrics.description: On filing each petition for the revival of an abandoned application, delayed payment of issuance fee, delayed response in reexamination, delayed maintenance payment, delayed submission of priority/benefit claim, or extension of the 12-month period for filing a subsequent application, $1,700.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may refund any part of this fee in exceptional circumstances as determined by the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension (petition) fees for 1-month extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: For petitions for 1-month extensions of time required by the Director: first petition $130; second petition $360; third or subsequent petition $620.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance fees schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees to maintain patents based on applications filed on or after December 12, 1980: 3 years and 6 months after grant $980; 7 years and 6 months after grant $2,480; 11 years and 6 months after grant $4,110.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless payment received by due date or within a 6-month grace period thereafter, the patent shall expire at end of the grace period. The Director may require a surcharge as condition of accepting payment within the 6-month grace period. No maintenance fee may be established for design or plant patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of delayed maintenance payments for unintentional delay
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may accept payment of any maintenance fee after the 6-month grace period if the delay is shown to the Director to have been unintentional and may require payment of the revival fee specified in subsection (a)(7) as a condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If accepted, the patent shall be considered not to have expired at the end of the grace period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect on rights of others when maintenance fee accepted after grace period
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent maintained as a result of acceptance of a late maintenance fee shall not abridge or affect the rights of any person (or successors) who made, purchased, offered to sell, used, or imported anything protected by the patent in the U.S. after the 6-month grace period but prior to acceptance of the maintenance fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A court may provide for continued manufacture, use, offer for sale, or sale under equitable terms to protect investments made or business commenced after the grace period but before acceptance of the maintenance fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent search fees and requirement to recover estimated average cost
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall charge specified fees for the search of each patent application (except provisional). The Director shall adjust the fees to ensure they recover an amount not to exceed the estimated average cost to the Office of searching applications by Office personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific search fee amounts are set by application type (e.g., $540 general, $100 design, $330 plant, etc.) as listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other processing/service fees (specific small fees)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall establish fees for other processing, services, or materials to recover estimated average cost, except specified services: for recording a document affecting title $40 per property; for each photocopy $0.25 per page; for each black and white copy of a patent $3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Yearly fee for providing a library with uncertified printed copies of specifications and drawings for all patents in that year is $50.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of fees for government requests and notice-related copies
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may waive payment of any fee for services or materials related to patents in connection with an occasional or incidental request by a government department or agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may provide any applicant issued a notice under section 132 with a copy of the specifications and drawings for all patents referred to in that notice without charge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustment of fees for inflation (CPI)
rubrics_metrics.description: The fees established in subsections (a) and (b) may be adjusted by the Director on October 1, 1992, and every year thereafter, to reflect fluctuations during the previous 12 months in the Consumer Price Index as determined by the Secretary of Labor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes of less than 1 percent may be ignored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for small entities — reductions and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to paragraph (3), fees charged under subsections (a), (b), and (d)(1) shall be reduced by 60 percent for any small business concern (per Small Business Act), any independent inventor, or nonprofit organization as defined by Director regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surcharges and other fees with respect to such entities shall not be higher than required of any other entity under the same or substantially similar circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional reduction for electronic filing for small entities
rubrics_metrics.description: The fee under subsection (a)(1)(A) (filing utility application) shall be reduced by 80 percent for entities eligible under the small-entity provision if the application is filed by electronic means as prescribed by the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refunds for errors and electronic data (Director authority)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may by regulation provide for a refund of fees in specified circumstances and provide refunds related to electronic patent and trademark data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text in source is truncated: the Director may provide for refund of part of fees for applicants who file a written declaration relating to electronic data; details left to Director regulations.
